status.en: 7 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 61% fewer than the week before, most of them in Juba, Abiemnom and Warrap.
status.nb: 7 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 61 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Juba, Abiemnom og Warrap.

summary.en: Violence persists across South Sudan, with armed groups ambushing civilians in Jebel Boma County and killing two people, and a road ambush in Warrap County killing five. In Juba, a central bank employee was killed, a plane crash left three survivors, and the airport manager was removed in an internal reshuffle. Women in Greater Mundri appealed for protection after attacks, while a Christian woman was killed after refusing a forced marriage to a Muslim man, and two pastors were injured in a separate attack. The Jonglei governor reported ongoing efforts to end clashes in Bor, Duk and Twic East, and elections were postponed again to February 2027. According to UCDP, there were two battle-related deaths in 2024.
summary.nb: Vold fortsetter i Sør-Sudan, med væpnede grupper som overfaller sivile i Jebel Boma fylke og dreper to personer, og et veipåkjøringsangrep i Warrap fylke som dreper fem. I Juba ble en ansatt i sentralbanken drept, et flystyrt etterlot tre overlevende, og flyplassdirektøren ble fjernet i en intern omorganisering. Kvinner i Greater Mundri ba om beskyttelse etter angrep, mens en kristen kvinne ble drept etter å ha nektet et tvangs­ekteskap med en muslimsk mann, og to pastorer ble skadet i et annet angrep. Gouverneur i Jonglei rapporterte pågående innsats for å stoppe kamper i Bor, Duk og Twic East, og valgene ble utsatt igjen til februar 2027. Ifølge UCDP var det to dødsfall i kamp i 2024.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
